Subject: URGENT: Cortex Health reserved throughput shortfall — need ops + exec plan (DH-4721)

Folks — Cortex Health (DH-4721) reported production impact: 95th pct latency ~1.8s, ~4% 5xx since 07:30 PDT. They are on a Reserved Capacity contract and expect predictable throughput.

What I have so far (quick summary):
- Customer: Cortex Health, US region, production traffic on /v1/generate endpoints.
- Symptoms: sustained latency spike, partial queueing, elevated 5xx. Customer attached error samples (see email).
- Billing/contract: Reserved plan; they expect guaranteed capacity up to committed QPS.

Asks:
1) Vivek — can you confirm whether the dedicated GPU pool backed their reservation is saturated / hitting headroom limits? We need current pool metrics (gpu utilization, queue depth, active sessions, model variants running) and what caused the sudden delta.
2) Jonas — if this is capacity/alloc issue, what’s the fastest operational remediation (quota bump, move to hot spare, temporary routing to compatible hosted model)? Please include change window and rollback.
3) Marissa/Neha — we should prepare an exec brief for CEO/COO + Cortex execs if we can’t provide a concrete ETA within 45 minutes. Also prepare customer-facing remediation commitment and a one-off credit proposal.

I’ve attached the customer samples and a pointer to the incident ticket: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-78934.

We’re on a rapid call at 09:40 PDT — please treat as priority.

— Priyom
(Internal: forwarded error samples and kpi-snapshot to ops)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: URGENT: Cortex Health reserved throughput shortfall — need ops + exec plan (DH-4721)

On Tue, Sep 7, 2026 at 09:36 AM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com> wrote:
> Folks — Cortex Health (DH-4721) reported production impact: 95th pct latency ~1.8s, ~4% 5xx since 07:30 PDT.

Quick ops readout:
- Root cause (preliminary): Dedicated GPU pool that services DH-4721 is saturated. We’re seeing a correlated spike in cross-tenant bursts from two non-reserved tenants that consumed a disproportionate share of remaining headroom after scheduled maintenance completed. The admission controller did not migrate enough capacity to the reserved lane fast enough — reservation enforcement lagged.
- Data: attached dedicated-pool-stats-0907.csv (current GPU util 98%, avg queue depth 64, tail latency 1.7s).

Immediate mitigations in progress:
1) Emergency allocation change: expand pool with +2 nodes from hot spare pool (ETA 12 minutes) — risk: brief reconnects for long-lived streams, low probability of 5xx spike during reattach.
2) Traffic shaping: enforce strict reservation tokens for DH-4721 (will evict/respond with 429 for non-reserved burst traffic) — ETA 6 minutes.
3) Fallback: route a small percentage of traffic to a compatible quantized variant with identical prompt-behavior (temporary model swap) to reduce per-token GPU work — ETA 20 minutes; requires customer opt-in for quality trade-off.

Ask leadership for authorization: approval to proceed with (1) + (2) immediately and (3) only if customer approves. If leadership wants a different commitment (e.g., instant quota reassign from paid pool), flag now.

I’ll update in 10 minutes with results of the node add.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Serving & Reliability
